paper.title: Orbital Abscess Complicating Allergic Fungal Rhinosinusitis Due to Streptococcus halichoeri: A Rare Zoonotic Sinonasal Infection.

BACKGROUND: Secondary bacterial infections complicating allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS) are uncommon but can be serious given the expansile nature of the disease which can thin and erode the bone separating the sinuses from the brain and orbits. Zoonotic pathogens are rarely implicated as pathogens.

CASE REPORT: A 21-year-old African American male with several years of progressive nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and hyposmia, presented emergently with acute left eye pain and swelling, diplopia, afferent pupillary defect and inferior visual field deficit. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute on chronic sinusitis with a left orbital abscess. The patient underwent emergent endoscopic sinus surgery with left orbitotomy and drainage of the orbital abscess. Intraoperative findings, pathology, cultures, and allergy testing were reviewed demonstrating AFRS and a novel zoonotic bacterium, Streptococcus halichoeri.

CONCLUSIONS: This case represents the first otolaryngologic case of S. halichoeri infection, a severe and complicated sinus and orbital infection. It is unclear if the severity of this infection was a consequence of the unusual pathogen, of the long-term thinning of the bone around the orbit, or both. Although AFRS is not considered an infection, secondary bacterial infection may occur and cause severe complications. Early surgical intervention and culture-directed therapy are essential in managing complicated sinonasal diseases.

OBJECTIVE: To explore the effects of four single-modality sensory stimulations on the brain functional networks in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (pDOC), and to clarify the correlation between different sensory stimulations and the improvement of patients' consciousness level, so as to provide references for clinical treatment and rehabilitation of pDOC patients.

A total of 57 patients with pDOC were enrolled and divided into visual stimulation group, auditory stimulation group, olfactory-gustatory stimulation group, somatosensory-nocieptive stimulation group, and control group. The intervention duration of each group was 15 min. Behavioral assessments were performed using the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS). Combined with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), hemodynamic parameters and brain functional connectivity were detected. Changes in brain function and consciousness level before and after different sensory stimulation interventions were evaluated.

RESULTS: Visual, auditory and olfactory-gustatory stimulations induced significant and robust alterations in cerebral activity across most detected channels (p < 0.001), while the cerebral response to somatosensory-nocieptive stimulation was relatively limited (p < 0.05). At the channel activation level, viewing family photographs in visual stimulation, light music, personalized music and family voice calling in auditory stimulation, and acetic acid stimulation in olfactory-gustatory stimulation significantly activated the corresponding brain regions (p < 0.05). At the brain functional connectivity level, viewing family photographs markedly enhanced functional connectivity within visual-related brain regions (p < 0.05); ethanol stimulation improved functional connectivity of olfactory-gustatory brain regions (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Single-modality sensory stimulation elicits acute cerebral activation in pDOC patients, which is superior to conventional rehabilitation alone. Visual and auditory stimulations exert significantly better intervention effects than olfactory-gustatory and somatosensory-nocieptive stimulations. Among olfactory-gustatory interventions, acetic acid stimulation produces prominent brain region activation, and ethanol enhances functional connectivity of related brain regions. Both can serve as an effective supplementary intervention for pDOC patients with visual and auditory dysfunction, and possess important value for further research and clinical application in the management of pDOC.

paper.title: Nuclear protein in testis midline carcinoma of nasal cavity: a case report and review of the literature.
paper.abstract: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) midline carcinoma (NMC) is an extremely rare, highly aggressive, and poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm that predominantly arises from the midline epithelial structures of the head and neck. It is driven by genetic rearrangements of the NUTM1 gene, with the most common aberration being a translocation that forms a fusion gene with BRD4 on chromosome 19p13.1. The diagnosis of NMC is challenging due to its non-specific clinical and histological features, and it typically requires a combination of immunohistochemical detection of NUT protein and molecular assays to confirm NUTM1 gene rearrangement. The prognosis of NMC is dismal, with a median overall survival of less than one year. To date, no standard treatment regimen has been established, and only individualized therapeutic strategies have been reported in the literature. Herein, we present a case of a 40-year-old female patient with NMC of the left nasal cavity who presented with nasal mass, nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, mild epistaxis, and hyposmia. The patient was diagnosed with NMC based on pathological and immunohistochemical findings, and was staged as T2N0M0. She received multidisciplinary treatment including neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radical surgery, adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) maintenance therapy. Up to the latest follow-up in February 2026, the patient had achieved complete remission with no evidence of tumor recurrence. We conclude that comprehensive and intensive first-line multidisciplinary therapy is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in patients with NMC, a disease with inherently high risks of recurrence and progression and a poor natural prognosis.

paper.title: Decoding the structure-flavor interplay of Lanmaoa asiatica under different thermal processing methods: Insights from multimodal analysis and molecular docking.
paper.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the differential effects of various heating methods on the structure and flavor of Lanmaoa asiatica. A multi-scale structure-flavor correlation approach combined with molecular docking was employed. The results showed that frying formed a dense outer crust and immobilized water, thereby promoting lipid cleavage and Maillard reactions, which contributed fatty, roasted, and mushroom-like aromas. Steaming loosened tissue structure and enhanced the release of polar small molecules, thereby highlighting fruity-floral notes. Boiling exhibited a "dual-low" profile of both precursors and flavor products. Four key volatiles (nonanal, phenylacetaldehyde, 2,4-heptadienal, 3-methylbutanal) were highly correlated with sensory phenotypes, and molecular docking suggested favorable binding interactions with specific olfactory receptors, mainly through aromatic stacking and hydrophobic embedding. These findings advance the understanding of flavor generation and release by integrating structural characteristics and water distribution, providing a theoretical reference for flavor modulation and processing optimization of edible mushrooms.

paper.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
paper.abstract: Motor vehicle collisions (MVCs) are among the most common mechanisms of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), and a meaningful proportion of affected individuals develop persistent post-concussion syndrome (PPCS) characterized by prolonged multidomain dysfunction. Conventional neuroimaging frequently fails to capture the underlying pathophysiology, leaving clinicians without objective diagnostic evidence. We describe a 57-year-old woman who sustained mTBI in a rear-end MVC in March 2023. Head computed tomography (CT) performed at the emergency department and a subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were both unremarkable. Despite normal structural neuroimaging, comprehensive multimodal functional assessment identified functional abnormalities across eight domains: vestibular function (videonystagmography (VNG)), cortical electrophysiology (quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG)), pupillary autonomics (automated infrared pupillometry), postural stability (computerized dynamic posturography (CDP)), oculomotor control (saccadometry), cardiac autonomic regulation (24-h heart rate variability (HRV)), olfaction (University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT)), and computerized concussion assessment (C3 Logix). Standardized psychological assessments confirmed moderate depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) = 14), moderate anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) = 12), clinically significant post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms (PTSD Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) (PCL-5 = 38)), and substantial headache impact (Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) = 58). The patient underwent a 10-modality individualized rehabilitation program. Concussion Symptom Checklist (CSC) scores declined from 92 at initial presentation to 0 by July 2023 (17 weeks post-injury), with near-complete re-resolution to 8 by February 2024 following a transient stress-related exacerbation. When conventional neuroimaging is unremarkable, comprehensive multimodal functional testing may provide evidence consistent with mTBI pathophysiology and help guide targeted rehabilitation. This case illustrates the potential value of a systematic, multimodal approach in PPCS management, while acknowledging that definitive attribution of findings to the index injury is constrained by the single-case design and absence of a pre-injury functional baseline.

paper.title: Integrated characterization of aroma, taste, and sensory properties of four commercial mutton soups from different regions of China.
paper.abstract: Mutton soups from different regions of China exhibit distinct flavor characteristics, but the chemical basis of these differences remains insufficiently understood. Five lipid oxidation-associated compounds were common to all products, whereas Guoshi contained relatively high levels of several spice-associated volatiles and showed the most distinct headspace fingerprint. Multivariate analysis identified ten potential discriminant volatile compounds. Jianyang had the highest total free amino acid and 5'-nucleotide contents, reaching 2125.44 and 66.89 mg/L, respectively. It also showed the highest equivalent umami concentration (5.802 g MSG/100 mL) and received the highest taste, aroma, and overall acceptability scores. These results provide a comparative basis for understanding flavor variation among commercial mutton soups and may support their quality evaluation and flavor optimization.

paper.title: Association of Abnormal Cerebral Perfusion in Very Preterm Infants With Late-Onset Sepsis and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes at 2 Years of Age: A Prospective Cohort Study Using Arterial Spin Labeling.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess cerebral blood flow (CBF) changes in very preterm infants with late-onset sepsis (LOS) using arterial spin labeling and their association with 2 years' corrected-age neurodevelopment.

METHODS: Fifty-six infants born at <32 weeks' gestation (LOS, n = 20; non-LOS, n = 36) underwent arterial spin labeling magnetic resonance imaging before discharge and Ages & Stages Questionnaires, Third Edition assessment at 2 years' corrected age. Voxel-wise CBF comparisons used family-wise error correction. Principal component analysis summarized regional CBF, and adjusted interaction models with simple-slope analyses evaluated CBF-development associations.

RESULTS: LOS infants exhibited lower CBF in the right superior and inferior orbitofrontal cortex, bilateral olfactory cortex, bilateral gyrus rectus, and left caudate nucleus (PFWE<0.05). Impairments were more prevalent in communication and personal-social domains (P < 0.05). The PC1 × LOS interaction was significant for personal-social scores (β = 7.19, 95% confidence interval 1.58 to 12.80; PFDR = 0.026), but not communication (PFDR = 0.317). The PC1 slope was positive in LOS infants but not statistically significant in non-LOS infants. Only the right gyrus rectus interaction survived regional correction (β = 7.96, 95% confidence interval 2.64-13.28; PFDR = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: LOS was associated with lower regional CBF, and associations of composite and right gyrus rectus perfusion with personal-social scores differed by LOS status, with positive associations among LOS infants.

paper.title: Rhythmic nasal air-puff as a potential noninvasive brain stimulation approach for stabilizing integrated brain network states.
paper.abstract: Breathing modulates neural oscillations and large-scale brain network organization, partly through mechanical stimulation of olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs). To investigate the mechanosensory contribution of olfactory input, we compared rhythmic, odorless nasal air-puff stimulation (~0.2 Hz) with oral breathing during resting-state fMRI in healthy adults (n = 21). Dynamic functional connectivity was analyzed using a hidden Markov model (HMM) applied to BOLD fluctuations centered on the stimulation frequency. Four recurrent brain states were identified, spanning a continuum from highly segregated to globally integrated configurations. Relative to oral breathing, nasal air-puff stimulation increased the fractional occupancy and lifetime of the integrated state characterized by higher global and local efficiency and lower modularity, reduced the overall switching rate, and selectively reshaped transition probabilities away from fragmented configurations. These effects partially reproduced key features observed during natural nasal breathing in our prior work, suggesting that rhythmic mechanosensory activation of OSNs contributes to the stabilization of integrated large-scale brain states. The findings support a respiration-entrained framework in which olfactory input contributes to the organization and temporal stability of large-scale brain networks.

paper.title: Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs.
paper.abstract: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are essential for insect olfaction, enabling the detection of carboxylic acids, amines, moisture, and temperature cues that mediate critical behaviors, including mosquito host-seeking 1,2. However, the structural mechanisms underlying ligand specificity and channel activation in these receptors remain unclear. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures and functional validation of the IR8a-IR75k complex from the malaria mosquito Anopheles stephensi, a carboxylic acid detector, captured in four states: the ligand-free full-length closed form (apo state), the ligand induced full-length open state, and the nonanoic acid (NA)- and octanoic acid (OA)-bound extracellular domains. These structures reveal a dynamic ligand-binding pocket in IR75k, in which specificity is determined by alkyl chain length and carboxylate geometry. Ligand binding triggers closure of IR75k's bilobed ligand binding domain (LBD), and this conformational change propagates through conserved mechanical linkers to the transmembrane domain (TMD), functioning as a molecular lever that dilates the pore via outward displacement of transmembrane helices. This gating mechanism was further corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiology. These insights provide an atomic resolution view of IR mediated host detection in mosquitoes and establish a foundation for the rational design of next generation mosquito control strategies targeting host-seeking behavior.

paper.title: Does depression in Alzheimer's disease show evidence of differential gene expression in neurons or microglia compared to Alzheimer's disease without depression?
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is common, distressing, difficult to treat and inadequately understood.

OBJECTIVE: We compared gene expression in neurons and microglia from AD patients +/- depression, stratified according to depression polygenic risk score (PRS-D) and looked for differential pathway regulation.

METHODS: We identified AD patients with (n = 95) or without depression (n = 25) whose brains had been donated to a UK brain bank. Exclusion criteria included other disorders known to affect cognition, previous major psychiatric disorder and a neuropathological diagnosis of a non-AD dementia. Depression was defined as a clinical depression diagnosis or Geriatric Depression Scale/Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale >7. PRS-D was calculated using LDpred2. In the AD + depression group, only the top (n = 29) and bottom tertile (n = 30) of PRS-D were analyzed by microarray. Tissue from superior frontal gyrus (SFG) and anterior insula (AIns) was sorted into neuronal and microglial fractions, and gene expression measured using a ClariomS Pico microarray.

RESULTS: After quality control, microarray data were available for AIns microglia (n = 51), AIns neurons (n = 59), SFG microglia (n = 60) and SFG neurons (n = 63). No individual genes had a p < 0.05, adjusted for false discovery rate. Gene set enrichment analysis identified significantly upregulated and downregulated pathways in both brain regions and cell types. More pathways were differentially expressed in microglia than in neurons. Many of these pathways related to infection or inflammation but also included olfactory transduction and Parkinson's disease.

CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion we have identified pathways that may contribute to the development of depression in AD. A majority were identified predominantly in microglia.

paper.title: Identification of candidate selenium-associated transcriptomic biomarkers in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an integrated bioinformatics and expression validation study.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is marked by long-lasting airflow obstruction accompanied by persistent inflammation and disturbed redox balance. Although oxidative stress is well established in COPD, it remains unclear whether PBMC transcriptional patterns that co-vary with a curated selenium-metabolism and selenoprotein signature can identify candidate COPD markers. We therefore evaluated such patterns as an exploratory transcriptomic prioritization strategy rather than as evidence of selenium-specific regulation.

METHODS: COPD-related transcriptomic datasets were downloaded from the GEO database, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were determined using conventional differential expression analysis. Selenium metabolism and selenoprotein (SMASP) genes were collected from the MSigDB. WGCNA was then used to identify a module closely associated with COPD status and SMASP scores, and candidate genes were defined by intersecting module genes with DEGs. XGBoost and SVM-RFE, together with cross-validation, were applied to select biomarkers. A nomogram was subsequently generated to assess their diagnostic utility. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and RT-qPCR validation were finally conducted to examine the potential involvement of these biomarkers in COPD.

RESULTS: We detected 235 DEGs and 40 selenoprotein-related genes, from which 17 overlapping candidate genes were obtained. ERBB4 and ZKSCAN3 were ultimately retained as biomarkers and were significantly decreased in COPD samples. The nomogram based on these two genes showed favorable predictive ability. GSEA indicated that both biomarkers were associated with ribosome and olfactory transduction pathways. ERBB4 was also linked to neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, whereas ZKSCAN3 was related to extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interaction. RT-qPCR in a small exploratory cohort (n = 5 per group) showed directionally consistent downregulation of ERBB4 and ZKSCAN3 in COPD samples, supporting the bioinformatics findings. This exploratory analysis was cross-sectional and does not establish causality, selenium deficiency, or clinical utility. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

CONCLUSION: ERBB4 and ZKSCAN3 were prioritized as exploratory candidate expression markers in the analyzed COPD datasets. Their diagnostic value, selenium specificity, and biological functions require confirmation in larger independent cohorts and functional studies.

paper.title: Association Between COVID-19 Vaccine Doses and Neurosensory Symptoms Among COVID-19-Positive Patients: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ageusia and anosmia are common manifestations of COVID-19. This study examined whether their frequency among infected patients was associated with the recorded number of Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine doses; it was not designed to estimate causality or vaccine effectiveness.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 5,348 COVID-19-positive patients over five years of age followed by the San Miguelito Health Region, Panama, from July 7, 2021, through November 2, 2022. Unvaccinated patients and vaccinated patients whose recorded doses were exclusively Pfizer-BioNTech were included. Separate logistic regression models estimated associations between vaccine dose category (zero, one, two, or three to four doses) and self-reported ageusia and anosmia, with two doses as the reference. A post hoc sensitivity analysis additionally adjusted for swab month.

RESULTS: Ageusia was reported by 507 patients (9.48%), and anosmia by 584 patients (10.92%). In the primary adjusted models, compared with two doses, adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for zero, one, and three to four doses were 1.87 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.48-2.38), 2.68 (95% CI 1.99-3.60), and 0.26 (95% CI 0.18-0.36), respectively, for ageusia, and 1.82 (95% CI 1.46-2.27), 2.53 (95% CI 1.91-3.35), and 0.18 (95% CI 0.12-0.25), respectively, for anosmia. After categorical adjustment for swab month, all six dose-category estimates were attenuated, and none remained statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Primary models identified strong associations between recorded vaccine dose category and self-reported ageusia and anosmia among infected patients, but these associations did not persist after adjustment for swab month. The results are compatible with substantial confounding by epidemic period and should not be interpreted as causal effects or estimates of vaccine effectiveness.

paper.title: Distinguishing the endotypes of Chronic rhinosinusitis: the emerging roles of macrophages.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disorder characterized by different endotypes classically known as type 1/2/3 inflammation. Recently, single-cell transcriptome analysis identified a series of macrophage subsets that have specific gene expression signatures associated with CRS endotypes.

AREAS COVERED: A literature search was conducted using PubMed with keywords 'CRS,' 'endotype,' and 'macrophage' and related terms, focusing on studies published over the past 10 years. This review dissects macrophage heterogeneity across CRS endotypes, summarizes how diverse stimulus factors shape macrophage states, and updates their roles under endotypes, providing clues for the development of macrophage-based biomarkers for endotyping and targeted therapy.

EXPERT OPINION: Effectively distinguishing CRS endotypes is meaningful for personalized therapies. An endotype-based interpretation of macrophage heterogeneity helps explain the divergent patterns of inflammation in CRS. In addition, the nasal tissue-resident macrophages attract growing interest as their contribution to olfactory loss in CRS.

paper.title: Environmental neurotoxicants as accelerators of brain ageing: exposomic mechanisms linking pollution to amyloidogenesis and Alzheimer's disease.
paper.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterised by progressive cognitive decline, amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic dysfunction, and chronic neuroinflammation. While rare familial cases are genetically driven, most AD is sporadic, underscoring the critical role of environmental determinants. Emerging evidence from epidemiological, experimental, and exposomic studies identifies environmental neurotoxicants, including air pollutants, heavy metals, pesticides, and emerging contaminants such as micro- and nanoplastics, as significant accelerators of brain ageing and AD pathogenesis.These toxicants access the central nervous system via systemic circulation, olfactory translocation, and gut-brain axis interactions, converging on shared pathogenic mechanisms such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired proteostasis, and neuroimmune activation. Together, these processes promote amyloidogenic processing of amyloid precursor protein, enhance Aβ aggregation, and drive tau pathology, accelerating neurodegenerative cascades. Notably, early-life exposures induce persistent epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, increasing lifelong vulnerability, particularly in genetically susceptible markers such as APOE ε4 carriers. Although preclinical models robustly demonstrate pollutant-induced AD-like phenotypes, translation into clinical interventions remains limited. Integrating environmental exposures into AD pathogenesis frameworks highlights the exposome as a modifiable risk factor and emphasizes the urgent need for longitudinal human studies, mechanistic validation, and preventive public health strategies targeting environmental risk reduction.

paper.title: Non-consumptive effects of Harmonia axyridis (Coleoptera: Coccinellidae) derived semiochemicals on Myzus persicae (Hemiptera: Aphididae).
paper.abstract: Biological control agents are central to Integrated Pest Management, where they suppress herbivorous pests through direct consumption. However, natural enemies can exert non-consumptive effects (NCEs) on prey when predation risk is detected, altering behavior, physiology, or life-history traits in ways that reduce predation risk but impose fitness costs associated with anti-predator defense. Often, NCEs reduce pest pressure on plants via risk-induced changes in herbivore prey feeding, reproduction, and immigration/emigration. Predator-emitted odors are important risk cues, yet predator-derived semiochemicals remain underexplored as tools for pest management. Aphid prey detect predation risk of lady beetles by eavesdropping on their odor cues. However, the specific semiochemicals that signal predation risk have not been explored. Here, we investigated whether a synthesized blend containing key pyrazine semiochemicals produced by the multicolored Asian lady beetle, Harmonia axyridis (Pallas), can induce NCEs in the green peach aphid, Myzus persicae (Sulzer). In Y-tube olfactometer assays, both alate and apterous M. persicae preferred to orient toward plant odors rather than toward plants with the synthetic methoxypyrazine blend. Exposure to the synthetic methoxypyrazine blend reduced aphid fecundity in laboratory and greenhouse arenas but did not alter aphid survival or induce production of alate morphs. In the greenhouse experiment, aphid populations were 27% lower on plants exposed to the synthetic blend by day 14. These findings demonstrate that predator-derived semiochemicals can induce NCEs in aphids, suggesting a promising area of exploration for a semiochemical-based strategy for Integrated Pest Management.

paper.title: Therapeutic Value of Budesonide Nasal Irrigation for Postoperative Maintenance of Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Real-World Study.
paper.abstract: Objectives: Budesonide irrigation (BI) has emerged as an effective postoperative topical therapy for chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS), providing improved drug delivery compared with conventional intranasal corticosteroid sprays. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of BI compared with saline irrigation (SI) in patients with persistent symptoms following functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) and to determine whether treatment effects differed according to CRS inflammatory endotypes. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 121 patients with CRS who underwent FESS between 2021 and 2024. Patients with persistent symptoms 3 months post-operation were treated with either continued SI (n = 54) or BI (n = 67) for at least 6 months. Clinical outcomes included changes in SNOT-22 scores, modified Lund-Kennedy endoscopic scores (mLKS), olfactory function assessed by KVSS II, oral corticosteroid (CS) use, and disease control status. Subgroup analyses were conducted for eosinophilic CRS (ECRS) and non-eosinophilic CRS (NECRS). Results: The BI group showed significantly greater improvement in total SNOT-22 scores than the SI group (p < 0.0001), particularly in rhinological symptoms. Endoscopic outcomes also favored BI, with greater reductions in total mLKS and mucosal edema scores. These benefits were observed in both ECRS and NECRS, although objective endoscopic improvements were more pronounced in ECRS. Patients receiving BI required fewer courses of oral CS (18.42% vs. 52.38%, p = 0.01) and demonstrated better disease control (p = 0.03). However, no significant difference was observed in olfactory function. Conclusions: BI provides superior symptom improvement, better endoscopic healing, and reduced oral CS use compared with SI during postoperative CRS maintenance, supporting its use in both ECRS and non-ECRS subgroups.

paper.title: Development of a Web-Based Nomogram for Predicting Survival in Patients with Esthesioneuroblastoma Using SEER Database.
paper.abstract: Background: Esthesioneuroblastoma (ENB) is a rare neuroectodermal tumor arising from the olfactory epithelium. This study aimed to identify survival determinants and construct a prognostic web-based nomogram to provide individualized survival predictions for ENB patients. Methods: Patients diagnosed with ENB between 2000 and 2022 were identified using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Patient demographics, tumor characteristics, and treatment data were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A web-based nomogram was constructed to predict 5- and 10-year survival probabilities individualized to a specific patient. Results: Nine hundred and forty-one ENB patients were analyzed. Overall survival (OS) rates at 1-, 2-, 5-, and 10-years were 89%, 85%, 75%, and 58%, respectively. Multivariable analysis revealed that age over 50 (p < 0.001) and tumor size over 6.0 cm (p < 0.01) were independent predictors of worse OS. Compared to patients treated with gross total resection (GTR) alone, worse OS was observed in those treated with chemotherapy (CT) only (p < 0.01), CT and radiation (RT, p < 0.01), GTR + CT (p < 0.05), RT only (p < 0.01), or no treatment (p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences in OS were found between GTR alone and GTR + RT, GTR + RT + CT, subtotal resection (STR), or STR with adjuvant therapies. The resulting ENB prognostic nomogram demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, with a C-index of 0.733 ± 0.041 and AUC of 0.749. Conclusions: Age and tumor size are critical survival determinants in ENB, and GTR continues to be the foundational treatment. The developed prognostic web-based nomogram successfully quantifies individualized survival probabilities, providing clinicians with a tailored tool to guide evidence-based counseling and management for ENB patients.

paper.title: Endoscopic Endonasal Approaches to Anterior Cranial Base Meningiomas: Indications, Limitations, and Surgical Decision-Making.
paper.abstract: Endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) has fundamentally changed the management of anterior skull base meningiomas by enabling access to many lesions through a direct minimally invasive corridor that avoids traditional transcranial exposure. Improvements in endoscopic optical technology, surgical instrumentation, and skull base reconstruction have steadily expanded the range of tumors that can be treated through an endonasal approach. Even so, EES is not appropriate for every lesion, making thoughtful patient selection and surgical team experience the most important determinants of surgical success. This review explores where EES fits in the contemporary management of anterior skull base meningiomas, including olfactory groove, tuberculum sellae, and planum sphenoidale meningiomas, with particular attention to its indications, limitations, and situations in which EES may not be appropriate. Evidence comparing endoscopic endonasal and transcranial approaches for anterior skull base meningiomas is reviewed, with attention to how tumor anatomy, oncologic objectives, and individual patient characteristics influence the choice of approach. A major consideration is how surgical morbidity can be minimized without compromising oncologic and safety outcomes. Current strategies to protect critical neurovascular structures, reduce the risk of cerebrospinal fluid leakage, and improve skull base durability, including advances in vascularized reconstruction techniques, are discussed. Emerging outcome data and the evolving learning curve associated with EES are also reviewed. Rather than presenting EES as a universal solution, the evidence points toward a patient-centered approach in which operative strategy and clinical decision making is guided by tumor characteristics, anatomy, and surgical goals.

paper.title: Gut Microbiome Alterations in TAAR5 Knockout Mice and In Silico Ligand Prediction.
paper.abstract: Trace amine-associated receptors (TAARs) are a class of G protein-coupled receptors with roles in olfaction, behaviour, and immunity. Known best as an olfactory receptor, TAAR5 has been linked to emotional behaviour and hippocampal neurogenesis, yet its peripheral mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given bidirectional influences between the gut microbiota and the host, we investigated whether TAAR5 deletion alters the gut microbiome in mice. Using 16S rRNA sequencing, we compared the gut microbiota of TAAR5-knockout (TAAR5-KO) and wild-type mice. paper.title: In Situ Cytokine Expression, Nitric Oxide and Reactive Oxygen Species Production During Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis Development.
paper.abstract: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), caused by Naegleria fowleri, is a rapidly progressive and fatal infection, and inflammation of the olfactory bulb plays a key role in disease pathogenesis. In addition, ROS and NO production increased throughout disease progression, indicating the establishment of a pronounced oxidative microenvironment. These findings demonstrate that N. fowleri infection induces a sustained local inflammatory response characterized by cytokine overproduction and oxidative stress. Together with inflammatory cell infiltration, these mediators may contribute to extensive olfactory bulb damage and disease severity, ultimately leading to host death.

paper.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: From Molecular Profiling to Personalized Clinical Management-A Systematic Review.
paper.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease imposing a substantial health and economic burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to address CRS complexity in both clinical and research settings. Thirty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Our results demonstrate that while AI-driven analysis helps stratify patient endotypes, the identified schemes exhibit substantial heterogeneity in cluster numbers and features, raising concerns about their reproducibility. AI applications also included histopathological image interpretation, drug discovery, biologic therapy selection, and prognostic modeling to evaluate revision surgery risks and olfactory dysfunction. However, using the PROBAST+AI framework, we found that 87.1% of the assessed studies carry a high overall risk of bias, mainly due to the reliance on apparent performance or internal validation and limited independent evaluation of model performance, indicating that many reported performance estimates may be optimistic. Future large-scale, multicenter collaborations integrating AI into clinical workflows will be essential to establish reliable and generalizable AI applications for personalized CRS management.

paper.title: Multimodal Plant-Animal Communication: Signaling Mechanisms, Coevolution, and Environmental Disruption.
paper.abstract: Plant-animal communication involves diverse forms of information transfer that can mediate ecologically important interactions, including pollination, seed dispersal, herbivory, and plant defense. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the chemical, visual, gustatory, electrical, acoustic, and vibrational information involved in these interactions, with particular emphasis on volatile organic compounds, herbivore-derived elicitors and effectors, multimodal signaling, sensory perception, learning, and evolutionary processes, including coevolution where reciprocal evidence is available. A central distinction is made between detectable traits or cues and functional biological signals, emphasizing the need for evidence linking signal production or modification to receiver detection, behavioral or physiological responses, and ecologically meaningful outcomes. Acoustic and vibrational phenomena are considered critically because their communicative significance remains less firmly established than that of chemical and visual signaling. The review further examines how climate change and other anthropogenic pressures may alter signal production, transmission, perception, and phenological synchrony, thereby reorganizing plant-animal interactions. Genetic manipulation of hormonal, volatile, and specialized-metabolite pathways is also evaluated as a potential tool for modifying plant signaling, together with its possible unintended ecological consequences. By integrating plant physiology, sensory ecology, animal behavior, evolution, and environmental change, this review identifies major evidence gaps and highlights the importance of plant-animal communication for biodiversity conservation, pollination, biological control, and sustainable agriculture.

paper.title: Biallelic PAX6 Variants in an Adult With Severe Microphthalmia and Preserved Intellectual Function.

Together, these findings expand the phenotypic spectrum of biallelic PAX6 disease and suggest that the homeodomain may have a tissue-specific role that is critical for eye development but largely dispensable for brain development.

paper.title: Vilazodone Hydrochloride-Loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carrier In Situ Gel for Intranasal Nose-to-Brain Antidepressant Delivery.
paper.abstract: The Oral delivery of vilazodone hydrochloride (VLZ), a serotonin partial agonist-reuptake inhibitor for major depressive disorder, suffers from extensive hepatic first-pass metabolism, food-dependent absorption, and poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, limiting its central therapeutic impact. Fourier Transform Infrared FTIR spectroscopy confirmed complete drug encapsulation, evidenced by disappearance of the diagnostic nitrile (C≡N) absorption band, while DSC and XRPD verified conversion of VLZ to an amorphous state within the lipid matrix. Drug release followed Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetics, sustained over 24 h, and the formulation remained stable under refrigerated storage. In Swiss albino mice, the intranasal NLC-in situ gel (1 mg/kg) produced a profound antidepressant-like effect relative to oral pure drug (10 mg/kg) across open field, tail suspension, and sucrose preference tests, consistent with enhanced nose-to-brain delivery via the olfactory and trigeminal pathways. Hence this nanocarrier-hydrogel strategy offers a promising, non-invasive route to enhanced CNS delivery of antidepressants.

paper.title: Nose-to-brain drug delivery: A new frontier in targeted therapeutics.
paper.abstract: Delivering therapeutics to the Central Nervous System (CNS) remains a major challenge in drug development, largely because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) limits brain exposure for most systemically administered agents. Among alternative delivery routes, intranasal administration has attracted significant interest because it leverages direct anatomical connections between the nasal cavity and the brain, thereby reducing reliance on BBB permeability. This review examines the nasal route, focusing on how olfactory and trigeminal neural pathways contribute to drug transport into the CNS. Rather than assuming a single dominant route, the relative roles of extracellular perineural diffusion, intracellular neuronal transport, perivascular movement, and cerebrospinal fluid-associated distribution are evaluated in light of existing experimental evidence. Key factors that limit or enhance intranasal brain delivery-including mucociliary clearance, local enzymatic activity, drug physicochemical properties, formulation design, and patient-specific variability-are discussed with attention to their practical implications. Recent advances in formulations, such as mucoadhesive and in situ gelling systems, particulate and lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, and stimuli-responsive platforms, are reviewed alongside developments in nasal delivery devices that influence regional deposition.

paper.title: Cerebrospinal fluid outflow pathways in neurodegeneration: nasopharyngeal lymphatics and the ocular glymphatic-like axis.
paper.abstract: The glymphatic system supports cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange and has been implicated, to different extents, in the transport or clearance of amyloid-β (Aβ), tau, lactate and other solutes. Although most studies have focused on CSF influx, astrocytic aquaporin 4 (AQP4) expression, perivascular localisation and polarisation, AQP4-mediated transmembrane water transport, and perivascular exchange, brain clearance also depends on efficient extracranial drainage of waste-containing fluid. In this narrative Review, we examine this 'outflow end', including meningeal lymphatic vessels, the cribriform plate-olfactory-nasal mucosal route, cranial perineural spaces, the nasopharyngeal lymphatic plexus, cervical lymphatic vessels and deep cervical lymph nodes. We highlight the skull base and nasopharyngeal lymphatic plexus as potential interfaces between intracranial CSF and extracranial lymphatic drainage and evaluate the route- and cargo-specific evidence for bulk-fluid and generic-tracer transport, soluble-protein clearance, aggregated-protein handling and immune-antigen drainage. We also consider experimental strategies targeting lymphatic contractility, VEGF-C-VEGFR3 signalling, mechanical stimulation, pressure gradients, AQP4-mediated transmembrane water transport and experimentally observed light-induced pupillary modulation. Throughout, we emphasise that evidence for individual cargoes, including Aβ, tau and α-synuclein, is uneven across anatomical routes and remains predominantly preclinical or indirect. Future studies integrating high-resolution lymphatic imaging, functional biomarkers and longitudinal or interventional designs are needed to determine whether altered CSF outflow is a consequence of neurodegeneration, a contributor to disease progression or a potentially modifiable process in neurodegenerative disease.

paper.title: Recurring and isolated intronic FGFR1 variants as an underdiagnosed cause of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder characterized by absent or delayed puberty and infertility due to gonadotropin-releasing hormone deficiency. METHODS: We investigated 4 unrelated families with CHH. Family 1 included a mother and 3 daughters presenting with variable reproductive phenotypes and incomplete penetrance of anosmia; Family 3 consisted of a girl with CHH and anosmia; and Families 2 and 4 consisted of male patients who presented with CHH and anosmia. Genetic investigations were done using either exome or genome sequencing. Experimental characterization of the identified intronic variants was conducted using RNA extracted from peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Exome or genome sequencing-based haplotyping was performed for the recurring variant.

RNA analysis confirmed that this variant generates a cryptic splice acceptor site, leading to the inclusion of 17 intronic nucleotides, resulting in a premature stop codon. Haplotype analysis revealed the variant occurred independently in each family. In Family 4, a distinct heterozygous intronic variant was identified in FGFR1, which was shown to cause intron 15 retention with premature termination.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that intronic variants in FGFR1 are a possible cause of CHH and can lead to diverse clinical phenotypes ranging from normosmic CHH to severe Kallmann syndrome, including significant presentation in female patients.

paper.title: The nose-brain axis as a neuroimmune conduit: how allergic rhinitis rewires the central nervous system.
paper.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) has traditionally been regarded as a type I hypersensitivity disorder confined to the nasal mucosa. However, persistent symptoms, nasal hyperresponsiveness, and comorbid neuropsychiatric disturbances-including headache, fatigue, cognitive impairment ("brain fog"), anxiety, and depression-cannot be fully explained by peripheral inflammation alone, thereby implicating the involvement of central sensitization. The nose-brain axis serves as a critical bidirectional conduit that relays peripheral inflammatory signals to the central nervous system (CNS) and initiates neuroimmune crosstalk, which is now recognized as a core driver of central sensitization in AR. In this review, we systematically delineate the hierarchical mechanisms by which the nose-brain axis mediates central sensitization in AR, encompassing: peripheral neuroimmune synapse formation, trigeminal afferent signaling, central integration within the brainstem and thalamus, functional remodeling of limbic and sensory cortical regions, microglial and astrocytic activation, central cytokine network dysregulation, glutamatergic hyperexcitation, and descending modulatory imbalance. We further summarize emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the nose-brain axis, including peripheral nerve modulation, suppression of central neuroinflammation, restoration of neurotransmitter homeostasis, and psychobehavioral interventions. This review provides a unified mechanistic framework for understanding neuroinflammation and central sensitization in AR and offers novel insights for developing targeted therapies for patients with refractory AR and central comorbidities.

paper.title: Immune Profiles and Immunotherapy Efficacy in Sinonasal Malignancies: A Scoping Review.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Little is understood about the efficacy of immunotherapeutic strategies against sinonasal malignancies (SN) or their immunologic profiles. This review summarizes key immune markers within SN tumors and underscores known data on the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors.

DATA SOURCES: The MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases were searched from database inception to present to identify studies on SN malignancies, including SN squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCCa), adenocarcinoma (SNAC), undifferentiated carcinoma (SNUC), and olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB), their immune profiles, and immunotherapy efficacy.

REVIEW METHODS: Included studies were those that either investigated the tumor immune profile (cellular or molecular) or reported findings following the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Two separate teams of two reviewers performed dual, independent screening and full-text review of 675 studies, with 52 included in the final analysis.

RESULTS: Anti-programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) immunotherapy is the most investigated immune checkpoint inhibitor against SN malignancies. Checkpoint inhibitor efficacy showed the most promise for SNSCCa with comparatively few studies in SNAC, SNUC, and ONB. TILs, not PD-L1 expression, most consistently correlate with survival in SNSCCa, SNAC, and SNUC. ONBs are predominantly immune-cold.

CONCLUSION: SN tumor rarity and heterogeneity limits research in immunotherapy efficacy and prognostic biomarkers. Multi-institutional research endeavors aimed at evaluating both checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and the SN tumor immune microenvironment are essential in advancing SN tumor management.

paper.title: Altered resting-state functional connectivity in lung cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is quite common clinically for cancer patients (including those with lung cancer) to have comorbid depressive symptoms. Numerous studies have shown that patients with depression often have altered resting-state functional connectivity (RS-FC). However, only a few studies have reported abnormal RS-FC in cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms. This exploratory and cross-sectional study examined a heterogeneously treated Chinese lung cancer population. Data on psychotropic medication, cancer-related symptoms, and detailed treatment histories were not systematically collected. The main objective was to observe the relationship between comorbid depressive symptoms and RS-FC in this population, which has not been reported yet.

METHODS: We calculated whole-brain RS-FC in 33 lung cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms and 42 age- and sex-matched lung cancer patients without comorbid depressive symptoms. The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) was used to assess depressive symptoms in lung cancer patients.

RESULTS: Compared to lung cancer patients without depressive symptoms, those with comorbid depressive symptoms showed altered RS-FC across eight brain region pairs: (1) left calcarine cortex-right cerebellar lobules IV-V, (2) left medial frontal gyrus-left anterior cingulate gyrus, (3) left insular-left middle temporal gyrus, (4) left precentral gyrus-left cerebellar lobule Ⅲ, (5) left thalamus-vermis Ⅰ and Ⅱ, (6) right olfactory cortex-right fusiform gyrus, (7) right rectus gyrus-right cerebellar lobule Ⅶ b, and (8) right cerebellar lobule Ⅶ b and right olfactory. Furthermore, total depressive symptom scores were negatively correlated with RS-FC between multiple brain regions, including the left superior frontal gyrus and right middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.72, p < 0.001), left superior frontal gyrus and left temporal pole middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.69, p < 0.001), left triangular inferior frontal gyrus and left temporal pole middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.65, p < 0.001), left medial superior frontal gyrus and right middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.65, p < 0.001), left insula and right cerebellar crus II (r = -0.6, p < 0.001), and right superior temporal gyrus and right cerebellar crus II (r = -0.67, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest preliminary associations between depressive symptoms and altered RS-FC in lung cancer patients, with connectivity changes correlating with symptom severity. However, because data on psychotropic medication use, cancer-related symptoms (e.g., pain, fatigue), and treatment details were not systematically collected, these findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive markers of comorbid depression. Future longitudinal studies with systematic assessment of medication, treatment, and multidimensional symptom burden are needed to determine whether these connectivity patterns specifically reflect depressive symptoms or broader cancer-related sequelae.

paper.title: The gastrointestinal KATP-ERK signaling axis: Molecular mechanisms, pharmacological opportunities, and emerging translational technologies.

BACKGROUND: ATP-sensitive potassium channels are metabolic sensors that couple intracellular nucleotide availability to membrane excitability, calcium signaling, mitochondrial function, and cell survival. Growing evidence identifies KATP channels as essential regulators of gastrointestinal physiology. They are expressed in smooth muscle, enteric neurons, interstitial cells of Cajal, epithelial and enteroendocrine cells, microvascular cells, pericytes, and liver, where they contribute to motility, secretion, barrier integrity, nutrient sensing, vascular regulation, and mucosal protection. In parallel, ERK1/2 are central effectors of the MAPK pathway, controlling epithelial renewal, inflammation, fibrosis, apoptosis, and tissue repair. This review proposes an integrated KATP-ERK signaling network that regulates gastrointestinal homeostasis.

CONCLUSIONS: The KATP-ERK-FGFR/Klotho framework links ion-channel pharmacology with gastrointestinal biology, providing a foundation for biomarker discovery, therapeutic development, and precision medicine approaches in gastrointestinal disorders.

paper.title: Outer Surface Functionalized Graphene Oxide Nanofluidic Platform for Selective Detection of Insect Pheromones.
paper.abstract: Invasive insects inflict severe ecological and economic damage, creating an urgent need for rapid and early detection strategies. Here, we present a biomimetic strategy that replicates the molecular recognition principles of insect olfaction. As a proof of concept, our platform comprises a graphene oxide membrane with its outer surface functionalized with the pheromone-specific odorant-binding proteins (OBPs) of gypsy moth (Lymantria dispar). The OBP selectively captures the pheromone, (+)-disparlure (DIS), in the vapor phase. This binding event alters the outer surface charge of the nanochannel, which is directly transduced into a measurable change in ionic current─a mechanism that enables vapor-phase molecular recognition using solid-state nanochannels. The sensor detects DIS vapor with exceptional selectivity against nontarget volatiles and a limit of detection of ∼121.7 ppm. It maintains robust performance over 24 days of storage at 4 °C and operates reliably across a wide temperature range (4-60 °C). Crucially, it selectively identifies a single live female gypsy moth within minutes, with no cross-reactivity to other lepidopteran species. By translating the selective mechanism of insect olfaction into a synthetic nanofluidic architecture, this work establishes a versatile and generalizable strategy for proactive pest surveillance in agricultural fields, forests, and border inspection stations.

paper.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: Recreational nitrous oxide (N2O) inhalation is increasingly prevalent among young adults, but acute psychiatric presentations following short-term binge exposure remain poorly characterized. We report a case of a female in her early 20s with no prior history of psychotic illness who developed an acute psychotic and dissociative syndrome over three days at an outdoor music festival. Her presentation followed heavy recreational N2O and 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) exposure combined with sleep deprivation. On admission, she exhibited profound disorientation, inability to recognize close family members, polymorphic delusions, passivity phenomena, and auditory and olfactory hallucinations, requiring involuntary psychiatric hospitalization. Diagnostic workup revealed normal brain and cervical spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and a normal electroencephalogram (EEG) without epileptiform activity or slowing. Serum homocysteine was moderately elevated (25.2 µmol/L) alongside a low-normal vitamin B12 concentration (270 pg/mL), consistent with N2O-induced functional cobalamin deficiency; both markers normalized following parenteral vitamin B12 and oral folic acid supplementation. During inpatient stay, treatment with risperidone was followed by progressive neutropenia, which fully resolved after cross-titration to aripiprazole. She gradually regained full insight, was discharged on day 12, and remained free of psychotic symptoms at her three-week outpatient review. This case suggests that short-term binge N2O exposure, together with MDMA and sleep deprivation, may contribute to severe neuropsychiatric presentations without chronic use; it illustrates the value of measuring homocysteine rather than relying solely on serum B12 levels; and highlights potential hematological adverse effects during antipsychotic initiation.

paper.title: Sensomics-guided decoding of key flavor drivers in six new superior table grape cultivars.
paper.abstract: Table grapes are high-value global berry crops, whose commercial value relies on cultivar-specific flavor quality. However, critical gaps in systematic flavor characterization of new superior cultivars restrict data-driven quality evaluation and flavor-oriented breeding. Herein, this study conducted comprehensive sensomics-based flavor profiling of six new superior table grape cultivars. The results showed significant inter-cultivar differences in appearance, color, and flavor composition. Electronic sensory analysis identified fruity/floral notes as olfactory markers and sweetness/sourness/saltiness as taste discriminants across six cultivars. Using GC × GC-QTOFMS, 270 volatile compounds were detected and 47 key odorants were screened via GC-O and OAV, with a six-attribute grape aroma wheel constructed. Recombination reproduced cultivar-specific aroma profiles, and omission identified 21 key aroma-active compounds, with (Z)-3-hexenal, (E)-β-ionone, and (E,Z)-2,6-nonadienal as core contributors across several cultivars. These findings reveal the chemical and sensory basis of inter-cultivar flavor differences in table grapes, laying targeted support for flavor-oriented grape breeding.

paper.title: Reversal versus classic stapedotomy for otosclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stapedotomy is the standard surgical intervention for otosclerosis, but the optimal sequence of surgical steps remains debated. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to compare the efficacy and safety of reversal versus classic stapedotomy for otosclerosis.

METHODS: A comprehensive search across five databases was conducted up to February 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized studies (NRS). The primary outcome was audiological success, defined as air-bone gap (ABG) closure to ≤ 10 dB. Secondary outcomes included continuous audiometric parameters and surgical complications. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) were pooled using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Ten studies (2 RCTs, 8 NRS) involving 1,540 patients were included. There was no significant difference between the reversal and classic techniques in achieving an ABG ≤ 10 dB (RR: 1.02, 95% CI [0.93, 1.13]). While statistically significant differences favored the reversal approach for postoperative ABG (MD: -1.57 dB, 95% CI [- 2.59, - 0.54]) and postoperative air conduction pure-tone average (MD: -1.86 dB, 95% CI [- 3.17, - 0.55]), these differences lacked clinical significance. Regarding safety, no statistically significant differences were observed, although the reversal approach showed favorable trends toward reduced floating footplates (RR: 0.23, 95% CI [0.04, 1.24]) and chorda tympani injuries (RR: 0.54, 95% CI [0.29, 1.00]).

CONCLUSION: Reversal and classic stapedotomy demonstrate comparable audiological outcomes, with no statistically significant differences observed in the assessed safety outcomes. However, the certainty of evidence was low for audiological outcomes and very low for complications, precluding definitive conclusions until further large-scale RCTs are available.

paper.title: Baseline sinonasal phenotypes in cystic fibrosis before elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor therapy: A cross-sectional analysis.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal disease is highly prevalent in cystic fibrosis (CF), yet pre-treatment disease burden remains incompletely characterized across CFTR genotype classes. As CFTR modulator therapy reshapes disease trajectories, establishing a genotype-stratified baseline of upper-airway disease before elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) initiation is essential for contextualizing subsequent sinonasal responses.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 45 individuals with CF underwent pre-ETI evaluation, including the SNOT-22 questionnaire, visual analog scale (VAS) for nasal obstruction, Lund-Kennedy (LK) endoscopic scoring, Lund-Mackay (LM) CT staging, and CCCRC olfactory identification testing. Disease burden was compared between heterozygous and F508del homozygous genotypes. Heterozygous patients were further stratified by the genetic class of the cystic fibrosis-causing mutation, ranging from class I to class VI, according to the type of mutation, and sinonasal outcomes were additionally compared by exocrine pancreatic status. Associations among symptoms, structural, and functional measures were assessed using Spearman correlations.

RESULTS: Mean VAS nasal obstruction was 4.15 ± 2.30 and mean SNOT-22 score 14.4 ± 11.2, indicating mild to moderate symptom burden. LK endoscopy showed mild to moderate disease (4.09 ± 1.54) and LM CT substantial opacification (14.17 ± 4.62). Olfactory scores varied widely (8.63 ± 3.08, D + E composite). No significant differences were found between genotype groups across any domain. VAS correlated strongly with SNOT-22 (ρ = 0.54, p < 0.001) and inversely with olfaction (ρ = -0.42, p = 0.02), but not with endoscopic or radiologic severity. Among heterozygotes, no domain differed between minimal-function and residual-function classes (VAS p = 0.129; SNOT-22 p = 0.177; LK p = 0.878; LM p = 0.225; olfaction p = 0.357), and none survived false-discovery-rate correction. Sinonasal scores likewise did not differ by exocrine pancreatic status, an analysis limited to 13 patients and therefore substantially underpowered.

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with CF exhibit measurable sinonasal disease across symptomatic, structural, and functional domains before ETI therapy. The absence of significant differences by genotype, by CFTR functional class, and by pancreatic status indicates that baseline upper-airway disease is largely independent of CFTR functional severity as conventionally classified. These findings establish a multidomain pre-treatment reference for future longitudinal assessment of sinonasal and olfactory responses to CFTR modulator therapy.

paper.title: The Biology of the Clonal Raider Ant (Ooceraea biroi) and Its Role as a Social Insect Model System.
paper.abstract: The clonal raider ant, Ooceraea biroi, is a blind, subterranean insect that combines several rare life history traits which make it uniquely suited for use as a laboratory model. The species has lost the queen caste; instead, colonies are composed entirely of clonally reproducing workers. Workers lay eggs in synchrony, giving rise to discrete and age-matched cohorts of new workers. Despite this simple biology, the clonal raider ant displays sophisticated social and collective behaviors, including scout-initiated group raids of live arthropod prey as well as regular colony emigrations. The species also relies heavily on pheromones and other olfactory signals to mediate general ant behaviors such as trail following, alarm responses, worker policing, and nonnestmate discrimination. Here, I discuss how the clonal raider ant provides unprecedented access to study these and other social insect behaviors with modern molecular tools.

paper.title: Robotic selective thoracic sympathectomy for hyperhidrosis: refined technique and anatomical variation.
paper.abstract: Primary hyperhidrosis substantially impairs quality of life. Conventional sympathectomy risks compensatory hyperhidrosis through trunk disruption, whilst selective sympathectomy preserves the trunk while dividing preganglionic and postganglionic fibres. We describe a technique refinement and a previously undescribed anatomical variant. A 23-year-old man had severe refractory palmar, axillary, plantar and gustatory hyperhidrosis (SSDS 4) profoundly affecting his confidence, social functioning and mental wellbeing, despite conservative management. He underwent staged bilateral robotic selective dorsal thoracic sympathectomy. Preganglionic and postganglionic fibres were divided from the top of T2 to T4 with trunk preservation. Refinements included resection from the top of the second rib, minimal diathermy with sharp dissection and non-touch technique using Maryland bipolar forceps. On the right, a postganglionic ramus ascending retrogradely from a displaced T3 ganglion into the third intercostal space was identified, previously undescribed in the literature, requiring dissection across the fourth rib to prevent hypothesized residual axillary hyperhidrosis. Both stages were completed 1 month apart, drain-free, with next-day discharge. There was complete symptom resolution, no Horner's syndrome and no compensatory hyperhidrosis at follow-up.

paper.title: Flavor evolution of Antarctic Krill (Euphausia superba) during thermal processing: insights from GC-IMS, GC-O-MS, and RATA.
paper.abstract: Despite its high nutritional value, the application of Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba, AK) is hindered by complex off-odors. This study integrated electronic nose (E-nose), gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS), and headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-O-MS) with Rate-All-That-Apply (RATA) to map AK flavor evolution under various thermal treatments, including steaming (100 °C for 5 min), frying (220 °C for 5 min), and baking (180 °C for 1 min). Based on the screening criteria of relative odor activity values (ROAV >1), and GC-O detection frequency ≥ 3, 29 key aroma-active compounds were identified. While raw and steamed AK exhibited mild, lipid-derived profiles, frying exacerbated fishy odors due to a surge in lipid oxidation markers (e.g., hexanal, 1-octen-3-ol, and 1-penten-3-one). Conversely, baking optimized the balance of Maillard-lipid interaction profiles, generating sufficient pyrazine-mediated nutty and roasty notes while avoiding excessive lipid oxidation. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) modeling confirmed that baking achieved the highest consumer acceptability, correlated with fruity, meaty, and caramel attributes associated with markers such as trans-2-cis-6-nonadienal, 2-propylfuran, and 5-ethyl-2,3-dimethylpyrazine. These findings provide molecular-level insights for developing sensory-optimized krill products, facilitating the high-value utilization of AK resources.
